definition: Integrity versus despair is Erikson’s last psychosocial stage, usually linked with later adulthood, in which people review their lives and confront whether they can see them as meaningful and fitting together as a whole. Integrity involves accepting one’s past, including gains and mistakes, with a sense of peace and self-acceptance, while despair involves struggling to reach that sense of meaning or completion.
